title: Pitch Sequencing
headline_insight: Pitchers repeat themselves most when they are behind: after a four-seamer in a three-ball count the very next pitch is another four-seamer 57.85% of the time, versus 43.23% across all counts.
what_it_means: Pitch selection is sticky, and stickiest exactly when the pitcher must throw a strike. When ahead the FF-to-FF repeat drops to 39.44% and the mix diversifies. Off-speed pitches self-repeat too, a slider follows a slider 35.35% of the time across all counts.
how_to_read: Each cell is P(next pitch type given the previous pitch type) within one plate appearance, one matrix per count-leverage class. Rows sum to at most 1; the remainder is next-pitch types off the top-8 axis.
why_it_matters: It is a readable Markov view of how sequences build, and it shows count pressure narrowing a pitcher's choices, descriptive context over 512,289 transitions.
caveat: DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY; strict pitch-number adjacency within a plate appearance; pitch_type is Statcast's auto-classified code. Not a predictor; no edge or ROI claim.
